title.id: Memahami Composition API di Vue 3 Tanpa Pusing
title.en: Understanding the Composition API in Vue 3 Without the Headache

excerpt.id: Refs, reactive, computed, dan composable dijelaskan dengan bahasa sederhana plus contoh kode yang bisa langsung dicoba.
excerpt.en: Refs, reactive, computed, and composables explained in plain language with copy-paste ready examples.

content.id:
Ketika pertama pindah dari Options API, saya juga bingung: kenapa harus `ref()` segalanya? Setelah beberapa bulan dipakai serius, Composition API justru terasa lebih *jujur* — data dan logika yang saling terkait bisa hidup berdekatan.

## Ref vs Reactive

Aturan mainnya sederhana: pakai `ref` untuk nilai tunggal, `reactive` untuk objek yang bentuknya memang seperti state.

```js
import { ref, reactive } from 'vue'

const counter = ref(0)               // angka, string, boolean
const form = reactive({              // objek form
  name: '',
  email: ''
})
```

Yang sering bikin tersandung adalah `.value`. Ingat saja: **di dalam script selalu `.value`, di template tidak perlu**.

## Computed untuk Turunan Data

Hindari menulis fungsi yang dihitung ulang di banyak tempat. Bungkus jadi `computed` supaya otomatis di-cache:

```js
const fullName = computed(() =>
  `${form.name}`.trim() || 'Anonim'
)
```

> Computed itu seperti rumus di spreadsheet: berubah kalau bahan bacanya berubah, tidak perlu dipanggil manual.

## Composable: Logika yang Dipakai Bersama

Bagian favorit saya. Ambil contoh hook deteksi scroll:

```ts
export function useScrollY() {
  const y = ref(0)
  const onScroll = () => (y.value = window.scrollY)
  onMounted(() => window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true }))
  onBeforeUnmount(() => window.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll))
  return { y }
}
```

Sekali ditulis, dipakai di mana saja — sidebar, progress bar, tombol back-to-top.

## Kapan Tetap Pakai Options API?

Tidak ada dosa. Untuk komponen kecil yang state-nya statis, Options API masih lega dan mudah dibaca. Tapi begitu logika mulai saling silang — fetch + polling + cleanup — Composition API jauh lebih rapi.

Selamat mencoba, dan jangan lupa TypeScript-kan composables kamu!
content.en:
When I first moved from the Options API, I was confused too: why `ref()` everything? After a few months of serious use, the Composition API actually feels more *honest* — related data and logic can live right next to each other.

## Ref vs Reactive

The rule of thumb is simple: use `ref` for single values, `reactive` for objects that are shaped like state.

```js
import { ref, reactive } from 'vue'

const counter = ref(0)               // numbers, strings, booleans
const form = reactive({              // a form object
  name: '',
  email: ''
})
```

The usual trip-up is `.value`. Just remember: **always `.value` in script, never needed in templates**.

## Computed for Derived Data

Avoid writing functions that get recalculated in many places. Wrap them in `computed` so they are cached automatically:

```js
const fullName = computed(() =>
  `${form.name}`.trim() || 'Anonymous'
)
```

> A computed is like a spreadsheet formula: it updates when its inputs change, no manual calls needed.

## Composables: Shared Logic

My favorite part. Take a scroll-detection hook:

```ts
export function useScrollY() {
  const y = ref(0)
  const onScroll = () => (y.value = window.scrollY)
  onMounted(() => window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true }))
  onBeforeUnmount(() => window.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll))
  return { y }
}
```

Write it once, use it anywhere — sidebars, progress bars, back-to-top buttons.

## When to Stick With the Options API?

No shame in it. For small components with static state, the Options API is still roomy and readable. But once logic starts crossing wires — fetching + polling + cleanup — the Composition API is far tidier.

Give it a try, and don't forget to TypeScript-ify your composables!
